sections.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE: 1 current-carrying / active part(s) have no model (U1), so a clean result here is not a clean bill. Draft models from their datasheets (`hauksbee models extract --unmodelled <board>`, or the Extend button in `hauksbee serve`), scaffold one by hand (`hauksbee models new`, then --models-dir), or supply BOM identity (--bom) to make this verdict conclusive. heads_up.what: A high-speed trace pair (DP / DN) is off its impedance target (W~0.150 mm, S~0.350 mm microstrip -> Zdiff ~ 146 ohm [target 90 ohm, USB differential]: estimate +62% from target).
heads_up.why: Fast links like USB (90 ohm differential) or Ethernet need their traces to present a specific impedance so the signal does not reflect off the wire and smear. This is a computed estimate, flagged only because the board did not formally declare a controlled-impedance stackup; it is informational, not a confirmed failure, but a value well off target on a real high-speed net can make the link marginal or fail to enumerate.
heads_up.fix: If this pair is NOT a high-speed link (USB/Ethernet/HDMI), you can ignore it. If it is: adjust the trace width and pair spacing for your actual layer stackup so the estimate lands near the target (the formulas are in https://hauksbee-docs.eoghancollins0.workers.dev/docs/checks/si_checks), or ask your fab to build a controlled-impedance stackup to spec.

heads_up.what: A single-ended trace (Net-(U4-LNA_IN/RF)) is off its impedance target (W~0.320 mm microstrip -> Z0 ~ 63 ohm [target 50 ohm, single-ended]: estimate +25% from target).
heads_up.why: A 50 ohm single-ended line is the convention for an RF or antenna feed: the trace has to present that impedance end to end or part of the signal reflects back instead of reaching the antenna, costing range and sensitivity. This is a computed estimate, flagged only because the board did not formally declare a controlled-impedance stackup.
heads_up.fix: If this is not a controlled-impedance RF path, this estimate is informational. If it is: widen or narrow the trace for your actual layer stackup so the estimate lands near 50 ohm (the formulas are in https://hauksbee-docs.eoghancollins0.workers.dev/docs/checks/si_checks), or ask your fab to build a controlled-impedance stackup to spec.

assumptions.statement: AE1 (Antenna_Chip) is treated as an open circuit.
assumptions.because: "Antenna_Chip" names a function, not a construction. A ceramic chip antenna is a DC open at its feed pad; a monopole or inductor-as-antenna is a DC short across its pads. Those are opposite answers to the one question this tool would ask of the part, and the generic value cannot say which applies, so this library states neither.
assumptions.consequence: Nets through AE1 are isolated in simulation, so any current path across it is missing from every result that depends on it.
assumptions.replacement: The actual part number. Its datasheet's DC continuity (ceramic patch = open, conductive element = short) turns into a one-line model card: an `ignore` entry for the open case, or a `passive` entry with the element's DC resistance for the conductive case. Put it in your models directory keyed on this board's value or footprint.
